findings.why: 'The first not fully gone' — I had to stop and work out that 'the first' meant her first orgasm; the phrase floats without an anchor.
The stacked 'under it... under that' ends on 'what the question had been for,' which is so abstract I paused to figure out what I was supposed to see on her face.
'Make the wanting mean anything safer' took a beat to unpack.

'The game' arrives here as if already established, and 'give that wanting air in daylight' plus 'pin it beneath a solemn name' piled two figures on top of each other; I went back to check I hadn't missed something.
Long, with the semicolon pivot to 'his own he would take last' — I had to supply the noun 'joy' and reorient.
'If pleasure was also a bridge' — a bridge to what? The conditional and the 'one fact' ending are abstract enough that I read it twice and still felt I was guessing.
'Her transgression' then 'theirs' in the next sentence — small hitch working out the ownership shift, though it resolves.
'As it went at everything on the quad' — the 'it' and the phrasing made me stumble before the hair description took over.
First appearance of the name 'Pace' after a long stretch of 'he' — a moment of 'who is this?' before I mapped it.
'Let herself hold that she wanted it' — the verb 'hold' is odd enough that I re-parsed the clause.
The dash-clause runs long and the 'grammar' metaphor with 'the labels and the lines and the correct shoe' took real work to assemble into the point being made.
'That, and the hand in his — it was enough.' Enough for what? 'That' points back vaguely; I paused to reconstruct.
The dance-follow metaphor is long and stacks several near-synonymous descriptions of tension; I tracked it but felt the length.
One long sentence carrying the kiss, the unwiped face, and her reaction — I had to hold a lot before the payoff.
Very long descriptive sentence; by 'ran the room while she did' I'd lost the grammatical thread a little and read on by momentum.
'Closer, but no.' — brief uncertainty about whose verdict this is and closer to what.
Enormous sentence, and 'the closed camel-coat project' refers to a woman who never appeared earlier — I stopped and searched back for a camel coat, found none, and had to let it go.
A fragment built on 'Now, after — not before... but after' with a nested colon and an italic-style question at the end; I re-read to sort the sequence of what she was doing.
'Randi giving half a head and enough weight' — I had to reread to understand this as her leading with her head/shoulder to stage the collision.
'Whatever sorority actually taught under the mixers and the letters' was a bump, plus it's the first I learn Randi is in a sorority.
The dash-interrupted syntax ('and — "Yes," she said... — kissed him') made me re-track the main verb.
